summary:
Beyond Signal is an educational platform and interactive simulation game designed in the style of NASA to teach space mission engineering and planning. Combining scientific space knowledge with practical engineering decisions ("Knowledge is the tool, decisions are the game"), the platform features 4 main modes:

Agency: Explores NASA’s history, centers, directorates, and key scientific questions.

Academy: A 5-level knowledge quiz testing mission understanding, complete with hints and a Leaderboard.

Mission Lab: The core gameplay where you turn a scientific goal into a spacecraft by balancing mass, power, communications, budget, time, and risk, then launch, simulate the journey, and manage unexpected events for a performance evaluation.

Studio: A tool to design, customize, and share your own space mission scenarios, constraints, and events.

Additional Features:

Historical Missions Study: Engineering analysis of iconic missions including Apollo 11, James Webb, Perseverance, and Artemis II.

Challenge Scenarios: Ranging from beginner (Cadet: CubeSat Pathfinder) to Flight Director (Deep Field Observatory).

Multiplayer (Crew Operations): Play solo or with up to 4 teammates via a shared room code, assigning roles (Mission Planner, Spacecraft Engineer, Science Lead, and Communications & Resources Officer) to make launch decisions together.
details:
Project Overview & How It Works

Beyond Signal is an interactive educational platform and space mission engineering simulator modeled after NASA’s operational philosophy: "Knowledge is the tool, decisions are the game." Rather than passively reading about space exploration, users actively step into the shoes of NASA engineers, scientists, and flight directors.

The experience is structured into four interconnected modes:

  1. Agency (Exploration & Foundation): Users explore NASA’s history, research centers, mission directorates, and the core scientific questions driving deep-space exploration.
  2. Academy (Knowledge Verification): A 5-level interactive assessment system that tests users' understanding of orbital mechanics, spacecraft subsystems, and mission logic. It includes smart hints to guide learning and a global Leaderboard to encourage healthy competition.
  3. Mission Lab (Core Engineering Simulation): The heart of the platform. Players select a scientific objective and must design a viable spacecraft from scratch. They face real-world engineering trade-offs—balancing mass, power generation, communications bandwidth, budget, development timeline, and mission risk. Once built, players launch the spacecraft, simulate its trajectory, and respond to dynamic, unexpected in-flight anomalies. At the end of the mission, a comprehensive post-flight debrief evaluates their scientific return, resource efficiency, and risk management.
  4. Studio (User-Generated Scenarios): A sandbox creation tool that empowers educators, students, and enthusiasts to build custom space missions—defining unique scientific goals, engineering constraints, and mid-flight events—and share them with the community.

Key Features & Creative Approach

  • Historical Missions Case Studies: Users can analyze the real-world engineering constraints and breakthroughs behind iconic missions, including Apollo 11, the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), the Perseverance Rover, and Artemis II.
  • Progressive Challenge Scenarios: Designed for all skill levels, starting from beginner missions (Cadet: CubeSat Pathfinder) up to complex, high-stakes deep-space operations (Flight Director: Deep Field Observatory).
  • Crew Operations (Collaborative Multiplayer): Space exploration is a team effort. Beyond Signal supports up to 4 players in real-time via a shared room code. Each team member is assigned a specialized role—Mission Planner, Spacecraft Engineer, Science Lead, or Communications & Resources Officer—requiring active communication and collaborative decision-making to achieve mission success.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Bridging Theory and Practice: Transforms abstract STEM concepts (physics, systems engineering, budget management) into tangible, cause-and-effect decisions.
  • Cultivating Systems Thinking: Teaches students that in aerospace engineering, optimizing one subsystem (e.g., adding larger scientific instruments) directly impacts others (increasing mass, power draw, and launch costs).
  • Accessible STEM Outreach: Provides a free, browser-based, high-engagement tool for classrooms, science clubs, and aspiring aerospace engineers worldwide to experience the realities of mission control.

Development Factors & Tools

  • Design Philosophy: Our team prioritized authentic NASA-inspired UI/UX telemetry aesthetics, clear visual feedback for engineering trade-offs, and low-latency multiplayer synchronization so teams can collaborate seamlessly.
  • Technical Stack: Built as a responsive web application utilizing modern frontend frameworks (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript/TypeScript), interactive state-management engines for real-time physics/resource calculations, and cloud-hosted room synchronization for multiplayer Crew Operations
